#!/bin/bash

# Remediation script for xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_rule_journald_compress
# Ensure journald is configured to compress large log files

if dpkg-query --show --showformat='${db:Status-Status} ' 'linux-base' 2>/dev/null | grep -q ^installed; then
    if [ -e "/etc/systemd/journald.conf" ]; then
        LC_ALL=C sed -i "/^\s*Compress\s*=\s*/d" "/etc/systemd/journald.conf"
    else
        touch "/etc/systemd/journald.conf"
    fi

    # Ensure file ends with a newline
    sed -i -e '$a\' "/etc/systemd/journald.conf"

    # Backup the original file
    cp "/etc/systemd/journald.conf" "/etc/systemd/journald.conf.bak"

    # Find the line number of the commented Compress directive
    line_number="$(LC_ALL=C grep -n "^#\s*Compress" "/etc/systemd/journald.conf.bak" | LC_ALL=C sed 's/:.*//g')"

    if [ -z "$line_number" ]; then
        # No commented Compress directive found, append to end of file
        printf '%s\n' "Compress=yes" >> "/etc/systemd/journald.conf"
    else
        # Insert the uncommented directive before the commented one
        head -n "$(( line_number - 1 ))" "/etc/systemd/journald.conf.bak" > "/etc/systemd/journald.conf"
        printf '%s\n' "Compress=yes" >> "/etc/systemd/journald.conf"
        tail -n "+$(( line_number ))" "/etc/systemd/journald.conf.bak" >> "/etc/systemd/journald.conf"
    fi

    # Clean up backup file
    rm "/etc/systemd/journald.conf.bak"

    # Restart journald to apply changes
    systemctl restart systemd-journald
else
    >&2 echo 'Remediation is not applicable, nothing was done'
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Ensure only one firewall service is active

# List of firewall services to check
SERVICES=("ufw" "iptables" "nftables")

# Function to check if a service is active
is_active() {
    systemctl is-active --quiet "$1"
}

# Function to check if a service is enabled
is_enabled() {
    systemctl is-enabled --quiet "$1"
}

# Identify which firewall service is currently active
ACTIVE_SERVICE=""
for service in "${SERVICES[@]}"; do
    if is_active "$service"; then
        ACTIVE_SERVICE="$service"
        break
    fi
done

# If no firewall service is active, enable ufw (default for Ubuntu)
if [ -z "$ACTIVE_SERVICE" ]; then
    echo "No active firewall service found. Enabling ufw..."
    systemctl enable --now ufw
    ufw enable
    exit 0
fi

# If multiple services are active, disable all but the first one found
for service in "${SERVICES[@]}"; do
    if [ "$service" != "$ACTIVE_SERVICE" ] && is_active "$service"; then
        echo "Disabling conflicting firewall service: $service"
        systemctl stop "$service"
        systemctl disable "$service"
    fi
done

# Ensure the active service is enabled
if ! is_enabled "$ACTIVE_SERVICE"; then
    echo "Enabling $ACTIVE_SERVICE..."
    systemctl enable "$ACTIVE_SERVICE"
fi

# Special handling for ufw (enable if it's the active service)
if [ "$ACTIVE_SERVICE" = "ufw" ]; then
    if ! ufw status | grep -q "Status: active"; then
        echo "Enabling ufw..."
        ufw enable
    fi
fi

echo "Firewall service remediation complete. Active service: $ACTIVE_SERVICE"

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Ensure only one firewall service is active (ufw for personal laptop)

# Check current firewall status
echo "Checking current firewall services..."

# Function to check if a service is active
is_active() {
    systemctl is-active --quiet "$1" 2>/dev/null
}

# Function to check if a service is enabled
is_enabled() {
    systemctl is-enabled --quiet "$1" 2>/dev/null
}

# Count active firewalls
active_count=0
ufw_active=false
iptables_active=false
nftables_active=false

if is_active "ufw"; then
    ufw_active=true
    ((active_count++)) || true
fi

if is_active "iptables"; then
    iptables_active=true
    ((active_count++)) || true
fi

if is_active "nftables"; then
    nftables_active=true
    ((active_count++)) || true
fi

echo "Active firewalls found: $active_count"
echo "ufw: $ufw_active, iptables: $iptables_active, nftables: $nftables_active"

# If ufw is already the only active firewall, ensure it's enabled and exit
if [[ "$ufw_active" == true && "$active_count" -eq 1 ]]; then
    echo "ufw is already the only active firewall. Ensuring it is enabled..."
    systemctl enable ufw
    exit 0
fi

# Disable and stop unwanted firewalls
if [[ "$iptables_active" == true ]]; then
    echo "Disabling iptables..."
    systemctl stop iptables 2>/dev/null || true
    systemctl disable iptables 2>/dev/null || true
fi

if [[ "$nftables_active" == true ]]; then
    echo "Disabling nftables..."
    systemctl stop nftables 2>/dev/null || true
    systemctl disable nftables 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# If ufw was not active, install and configure it
if [[ "$ufw_active" == false ]]; then
    echo "Installing/ensuring ufw is available..."
    apt-get update -qq
    apt-get install -y ufw
    
    # Reset ufw to default state
    ufw --force reset
    
    # Set default policies
    ufw default deny incoming
    ufw default allow outgoing
    
    # Enable ufw
    ufw --force enable
fi

# Ensure ufw is enabled and started
systemctl enable ufw
systemctl start ufw

# Verify final state
echo "Verifying final firewall state..."
systemctl status ufw --no-pager || true

# Final check
final_active=0
systemctl is-active --quiet ufw && ((final_active++)) || true
systemctl is-active --quiet iptables && ((final_active++)) || true
systemctl is-active --quiet nftables && ((final_active++)) || true

if [[ "$final_active" -eq 1 && "$(systemctl is-active ufw)" == "active" ]]; then
    echo "SUCCESS: Only ufw is active."
    exit 0
else
    echo "ERROR: Firewall state is not as expected. Active firewalls: $final_active"
    exit 1
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Define firewall services to consider
declare -a FIREWALL_SERVICES=(
    "ufw"
    "netfilter-persistent"   # iptables-persistent service
    "nftables"
)

# Helper to check if a systemd unit exists
unit_exists() {
    systemctl list-unit-files "$1" &>/dev/null
}

# Determine which services are active
declare -A ACTIVE_SERVICES
active_count=0
for svc in "${FIREWALL_SERVICES[@]}"; do
    if unit_exists "$svc.service"; then
        if systemctl is-active --quiet "$svc.service"; then
            ACTIVE_SERVICES["$svc"]=1
            ((active_count++))
        fi
    fi
done

# Desired primary firewall
PRIMARY="ufw"

# Ensure the primary firewall service exists; if not, fall back to the first active one
if ! unit_exists "$PRIMARY.service"; then
    # pick first active service as primary
    for svc in "${!ACTIVE_SERVICES[@]}"; do
        PRIMARY="$svc"
        break
    done
fi

# If no firewall is active, enable the primary
if (( active_count == 0 )); then
    if unit_exists "$PRIMARY.service"; then
        echo "No firewall active. Enabling and starting $PRIMARY."
        systemctl enable --now "$PRIMARY.service"
    else
        echo "Error: No firewall service found to enable." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    exit 0
fi
